docs.title: StudFinder
docs.text:
Upload a photo of a LEGO piece. Find it on BrickLink.

StudFinder is a Docker-based Python web app that identifies LEGO parts, sets, minifigures, and sticker sheets from photographs. It chains three free/public APIs together to give you instant identification, catalog details, and current market pricing.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
You upload a photo
    ↓
Brickognize API — identifies the item (98.5% accuracy, 125k catalog)
    ↓
Rebrickable API — enriches with category, set appearances
    ↓
BrickLink API — fetches current new/used prices and seller counts
    ↓
You see match results with images, prices, and direct links

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Image recognition — identify parts, sets, minifigs, and sticker sheets from a photo
  • Drag-and-drop UI — polished dark-theme interface with preview and skeleton loading
  • Market pricing — real-time new/used prices from BrickLink (when configured)
  • Set appearances — see which sets a part appears in
  • Graceful degradation — each API is independent; if one fails, you still get partial results
  • Docker single-container — one docker compose up and you're running

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker (Engine + Compose)
  • A free Rebrickable API key
  • (Optional) BrickLink API OAuth credentials for pricing

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone <your-repo>
cd StudFinder
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env with your API keys
docker compose up -d
open http://localhost:8000

Get started →{ .md-button .md-button--primary } View on GitHub :fontawesome-brands-github:{ .md-button }

docs.title: POST /upload
docs.text: Upload an image for LEGO part identification.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

Field Type Required Description file Image (JPEG/PNG) Yes Photo of a LEGO piece

Example using curl:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/upload \
  -F "file=@photo.jpg"

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description matches array List of identified items, ordered by confidence (descending) matches[].item_no string BrickLink / Rebrickable item number matches[].name string Human-readable item name matches[].item_type string PART, SET, MINIFIG, or STICKER_SHEET matches[].category string Category name (e.g. "Brick", "Plate") matches[].confidence float Match confidence score (0.0 – 1.0) matches[].thumbnail_url string Thumbnail image URL matches[].bricklink_url string Direct link to BrickLink catalog page matches[].rebrickable_url string Direct link to Rebrickable page matches[].set_appearances array Up to 5 sets this part appears in (parts only) matches[].pricing object Current BrickLink price guide (null if unconfigured) processing_time float Server-side processing time in seconds

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
1. User drags an image onto the upload zone in the browser
  2. Browser shows a local preview and sends a POST /upload with the file
  3. FastAPI reads the image bytes and calls Brickognize API
  4. Brickognize returns up to 5 candidate matches with item numbers and confidence scores
  5. For each match, FastAPI calls Rebrickable and BrickLink in parallel:
    • Rebrickable resolves the part name, category, and set appearances
    • BrickLink fetches current new/used pricing
  6. FastAPI merges all data into an enriched response
  7. Browser renders result cards with images, badges, pricing, and links

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Each external call is wrapped in its own try/except. If any API fails: - Brickognize failure → empty results (nothing to show) - Rebrickable failure → fall back to Brickognize's name, no set appearances - BrickLink failure → no pricing shown, card still renders

This means the app works even with minimal configuration (Brickognize only).

docs.title: File layout
docs.text:
app/
├── main.py           # FastAPI app, static file mount
├── config.py         # Pydantic Settings from env
├── router.py         # Route handlers
├── models.py         # Pydantic response/request models
├── brickognize.py    # Async HTTP client
├── rebrickable.py    # Async HTTP client
└── bricklink.py      # Sync OAuth 1.0 client (offloaded to thread)

docs.title: Why sync for BrickLink?
docs.text: The BrickLink API uses OAuth 1.0. The requests-oauthlib library (which handles the signing) is synchronous. Rather than reimplementing OAuth 1.0 signing for httpx, the call is offloaded to a thread pool with asyncio.to_thread so it doesn't block the event loop.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All configuration is via environment variables (loaded from .env at startup).

docs.title: REBRICKABLE_API_KEY
docs.text:
:material-required: Required

Your Rebrickable API key. Get one for free at rebrickable.com/api.

REBRICKABLE_API_KEY=abc123def456abc789def012abc345de

Controls: part name resolution, category lookup, set appearance data.

docs.title: BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_KEY
docs.text:
:material-optional: Optional

Your BrickLink OAuth 1.0 consumer key. Requires applying at bricklink.com/v3/api.register.html.

BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_KEY=your_key_here

docs.title: BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_SECRET
docs.text:
:material-optional: Optional

Your BrickLink OAuth 1.0 consumer secret.

BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_SECRET=your_secret_here

docs.title: BRICKLINK_TOKEN_VALUE
docs.text:
:material-optional: Optional

Your BrickLink OAuth 1.0 token value (access token).

BRICKLINK_TOKEN_VALUE=your_token_here

docs.title: BRICKLINK_TOKEN_SECRET
docs.text:
:material-optional: Optional

Your BrickLink OAuth 1.0 token secret.

BRICKLINK_TOKEN_SECRET=your_token_secret_here

docs.title: HOST
docs.text:
:material-optional: Optional (default: 0.0.0.0)

The host address the uvicorn server binds to.

HOST=0.0.0.0

docs.title: PORT
docs.text:
:material-optional: Optional (default: 8000)

The port the uvicorn server listens on.

PORT=8000

docs.title: Sample .env file
docs.text:
REBRICKABLE_API_KEY=abc123def456abc789def012abc345de
BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_KEY=ck_xxxxxxxxxxxx
BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_SECRET=cs_xxxxxxxxxxxx
BRICKLINK_TOKEN_VALUE=tv_xxxxxxxxxxxx
BRICKLINK_TOKEN_SECRET=ts_xxxxxxxxxxxx
HOST=0.0.0.0
PORT=8000

docs.title: Graceful degradation
docs.text:
Each external API is independent:

Service missing What you lose Rebrickable key Part name falls back to Brickognize name, no category, no set appearances BrickLink credentials No pricing data (new/used prices, seller counts) Both App still identifies parts via Brickognize and links to BrickLink/Rebrickable

docs.title: Local setup (without Docker)
docs.text:
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate   # or venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 on Windows
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env with your API keys
uvicorn app.main:app --reload

The --reload flag enables hot-reload when source files change.

docs.title: Building the docs site
docs.text:
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs build

Output goes to site/. To preview locally:

mkdocs serve
# Open http://localhost:8001

docs.title: Deploying docs to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
mkdocs gh-deploy

This builds the site and pushes the site/ directory to the gh-pages branch. GitHub Pages must be configured to serve from gh-pages in your repo settings.

docs.title: Adding a new external API
docs.text:
1. Create a new module in app/ (e.g. app/example.py)
  2. Add an async function that returns the data
  3. Call it from router.py — wrap in try/except for graceful degradation
  4. Add the response data to EnrichedMatch in models.py
  5. Update the frontend to display it

docs.title: Default (docker compose)
docs.text:
docker compose up -d

This builds the image and starts the container. The app is available at http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Manual docker build
docs.text:
docker build -t studfinder .
docker run -d -p 8000:8000 --env-file .env --name studfinder studfinder

docs.title: Stop
docs.text: docker compose down

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

The image uses python:3.12-slim as a lightweight base. Dependencies are cached by copying requirements.txt first — the layer is reused unless dependencies change.

docs.title: docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
services:
  studfinder:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    env_file:
      - .env
    restart: unless-stopped

Environment variables are loaded from .env. The container restarts automatically unless explicitly stopped.

docs.title: Port mapping
docs.text:
To use a different port on the host:

# docker compose
ports:
  - "9000:8000"

# docker run
docker run -d -p 9000:8000 ...

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/danvargic/StudFinder.git
cd StudFinder

docs.title: 2. Set up API credentials
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and fill in your keys:

cp .env.example .env

docs.title: Rebrickable API key (required)
docs.text:
1. Go to rebrickable.com/api
  2. Create a free account
  3. Copy your API key
  4. Add it to .env:
REBRICKABLE_API_KEY=your_32_char_hex_key

docs.title: BrickLink API credentials (optional — enables pricing)
docs.text:
BrickLink pricing data requires OAuth 1.0 credentials. Apply at bricklink.com/v3/api.register.html.

Once approved, add to .env:

BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_KEY=your_consumer_key
BRICKLINK_CONSUMER_SECRET=your_consumer_secret
BRICKLINK_TOKEN_VALUE=your_token_value
BRICKLINK_TOKEN_SECRET=your_token_secret

Note

Without BrickLink credentials the app still works — you'll get identification and Rebrickable data, just no pricing.

docs.title: 3. Start the app
docs.text:
docker compose up -d

This builds the image (if needed) and starts the container on port 8000.

docs.title: 4. Open the UI
docs.text:
http://localhost:8000

Drag a photo of a LEGO piece onto the upload zone. Results appear within seconds.

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text: Item type Works? LEGO parts (bricks, plates, tiles, etc.) ✅ LEGO sets (boxed sets) ✅ Minifigures ✅ Sticker sheets ✅ Non-LEGO items ❌ (may give false positives)

docs.title: Tips for best results
docs.text:
• Place the piece on a plain, contrasting background (white or black)
  • Use good, even lighting — avoid harsh shadows
  • Photograph the piece from the top in a clear, focused shot
  • For printed/stickered pieces, make sure the print is visible
